class.name: TerrainDataMap3D
class.brief_description: Terrain analysis maps for placing vegetation: slope, curvature, flow, wetness, water depth and distance to water.
class.description: Bakes terrain analysis maps over a square of [member size] metres centred on the node, [member resolution] cells a side, for placement rules (grass on gentle slopes, reeds where the ground is wet, trees away from water) and materials. Heights come from [member height_source] or from rays down against [member ground_collision_mask]. Water comes from [member water_sources]. The maps are: - slope and aspect (Horn 1981), - curvature (Zevenbergen and Thorne 1987, positive in hollows), - flow accumulation (multiple flow direction over a depression-filled surface, Priority-Flood), - topographic wetness index [code]ln(a / tan(slope))[/code] (Beven and Kirkby 1979), - water depth and signed distance to water. Query them on the CPU with the [code]get_*_at[/code] methods, or in shaders through the global uniforms described in [method get_shader_code]. Baking runs on the CPU once; it has no per-frame cost.

method.name: bake
method.description: Samples heights and water and computes every map. Returns [constant ERR_UNCONFIGURED] when no height could be found. Emits [signal baked].

method.name: get_aspect_at
method.description: Direction the ground faces (downhill), in radians from +Z clockwise towards +X, at the nearest cell.

method.name: get_bake_time_msec
method.description: Time the last [method bake] took, in milliseconds.

method.name: get_channel_image
method.description: Returns one map as a single-channel float [Image] ([constant Image.FORMAT_RF]), row 0 at the map's lowest Z.

method.name: get_curvature_at
method.description: Zevenbergen-Thorne general curvature in 1/m: positive in hollows and valley floors where water collects, negative on ridges.

method.name: get_data_texture
method.description: RGBA float texture: height, slope (radians), aspect (radians), curvature (1/m).

method.name: get_flow_at
method.description: Flow accumulation: log10 of the upslope area in square metres that drains through this point. Flow ends in water, so ground beside a river only collects its own slope.

method.name: get_height_at
method.description: Ground height sampled during the bake.

method.name: get_map_rect
method.description: The baked area in world XZ (position is the corner at the lowest X and Z).

method.name: get_shader_code
method.description: Shader code that declares the global uniforms [code]terrain_data_map[/code], [code]terrain_water_map[/code] and [code]terrain_data_rect[/code] and the functions [code]terrain_data(world_pos)[/code] (height, slope, aspect, curvature) and [code]terrain_water(world_pos)[/code] (flow, wetness, water depth, signed distance to water). Paste it into a spatial or compute shader. The uniforms are set when [member publish_shader_globals] is on.

method.name: get_water_depth_at
method.description: Water depth in metres, 0 on land.

method.name: get_water_distance_at
method.description: Signed distance to the shoreline in metres: positive on land, negative under water. [code]1000000[/code] when the map has no water.

method.name: get_water_texture
method.description: RGBA float texture: flow (log10 m²), wetness index, water depth (m), signed distance to water (m).

method.name: get_wetness_at
method.description: Topographic wetness index [code]ln(a / tan(slope))[/code], a = upslope area per metre of contour. Higher is wetter: about 4 to 7 on hillsides, 10 and above on flat ground where water collects (meadows, swamps).

method.name: queue_bake
method.description: Bakes at the end of the frame, once, however many times it is called.

members.member: Bake one frame after the node is ready (not in the editor), once terrain deformers and colliders are in place.
Exponent of the slope weight in multiple flow direction routing (Holmgren 1994). Around 1.1 spreads flow over hillsides like real overland flow; higher values concentrate it into channels.
Physics layers hit by the rays used where [member height_source] gives no height.

Node that gives ground heights: a [TerrainDeformer3D], any node with [code]get_height(Vector3)[/code], or a Terrain3D node (its [code]get_data().get_height()[/code]). Empty: rays against [member ground_collision_mask].
Set the global shader uniforms from [method get_shader_code] after each bake.
Cells per side. The cell size is [member size] / [member resolution].
Width of the square map in metres, centred on the node.

Water nodes. A node with [code]get_water_level()[/code] (a water surface, sea or lake) is a level plane at its height plus that level, covering all lower ground in the map; its waves are left out. Otherwise a node with [code]sample_height(Vector3)[/code] (such as a river) gives its surface height, -INF outside it. A river that also has [code]get_section_count()[/code] and [code]get_section(index)[/code] ([PhysXRiver3D]) is only asked about the cells near its channel, so world-size maps bake in seconds.

constants.constant: Signed distance to water in metres.
